content:
marcos: incident-bot just posted a SEV2 for inference-hosted-us-east — 95th p95 latency jumped from ~2s to ~6s and some 5xxs seen by customers. paging flow looks fuzzy for the midnight swap window. tagging primary/secondary and asking for runbook pointers. can someone confirm who is primary right now?

incident-bot: [AUTO] SEV2 triggered — latency anomaly on inference-hosted-us-east. Alert ID: inc-20260304-81. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Initial detection at 02:03 UTC.

jamie: I'm primary for the midnight window — I got the pager @ 02:04. currently looking at tail logs. seeing many KV-cache misses and steady CPU on the cudnn nodes.

tara: I was listed as secondary in the roster but wasn't paged. roster link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/oncall-roster (we should confirm pager bindings).

marcos: ok — thank you. we need clear escalation timing for these windows: if primary doesn't ack in X minutes, who gets paged, phone escalation rules, etc. SEV2/SEV1 distinctions. current customer impact: a handful of paying customers reporting >3s TTF in the last 10 minutes and a few requests 502ing.

jamie: quick triage notes —
- p95 spike correlates with sustained queue depth on the inference-forwarder (queue > 200).
- backend pods are restarting slowly (OOMKill spikes on model-quant pod).
- attempted scale up but HPA didn't react quick enough.

jamie: mitigation plan I'm executing now:
1) scale model-count to 10 replicas:
```
kubectl scale deploy inference-model-quant -n prod --replicas=10
```
2) flip routing to fallback-model-v1 for high-latency routes:
```
redwoodctl route set --service inference --fallback-model=fallback-model-v1
```
3) if no improvement in 6m, hand off to tara and escalate pager to SRE lead.

alice: quick note — runbook for "inference latency spike" is here: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/inference-latency.md. relevant excerpt: "Pager flow: primary -> 8m -> secondary -> 20m -> SRE lead -> 30m -> ENG manager/SEV bridge for customer-facing comms". can we standardize those timings for midnight swaps?

marcos: that excerpt is helpful. proposal: shorten the first escalation window during high-traffic swaps. suggested: primary -> 6m -> secondary -> 12m -> sre-lead -> 20m -> eng-manager (phone). these are only for windows labeled "swap-surge" in schedule.

devops-lead: +1 on shorter windows for swap windows. also add a quick phone escalation for any sustained >30% error-rate for paid customers. policy to add in runbook:
- SEV1 (customer-facing outage): immediate phone to SRE lead and ENG manager after 2m if no ack.
- SEV2 (degraded): primary 0m, escalate to secondary at 6m, escalate to SRE lead at 12m.

tara: confirming I will take over if jamie needs to step out. jamie — if you hand off, please post small summary of actions & point to the in-progress `kubectl` commands so I can pick up.

jamie: agreed. current status: scaled to 10, route flipped at 02:07. p95 dropped from 6.1s -> 3.4s within 90s, errors reduced but still ~0.8% 5xx. leaving auto-scaling watch for next 10m.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] Alert inc-20260304-81: mitigation actions detected. Event log: scale action by jamie at 02:07, route flip at 02:08.

marcos: customer impact note for the log: affected customers were two mid-market tenants on prod (tenant-phi and tenant-rho). recommend sending a brief post-incident note if we don't fully resolve within the hour.

jamie: tagging the runbook snippet I'm following:
> Pager flow (default): primary -> 8m -> secondary -> 20m -> SRE lead -> eng-manager phone at 30m
> Pager flow (swap-surge override): primary -> 6m -> secondary -> 12m -> SRE lead -> eng-manager phone at 20m

marcos: decision log: we agree to adopt the swap-surge override windows for tonight's swap period (00:00–06:00 UTC). jamie remains primary, tara secondary. devops-lead will be on-call for phone escalation if SRE lead is unreachable. action items:
- jamie: monitor for 20m and call devops-lead if errors >1% persist.
- tara: stand ready to take over; on ack escalate per new timings.
- alice: update runbook with the swap-surge timings and publish.

alice: will update runbook now and ping #release when done. also adding a short checklist for handoffs: current primary, secondary, active mitigations, command history, customer list.

jamie: final note before handoff: keep `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=inference -o wide` handy. if we see OOM spikes, consider temporary JVM flag tweak in model-quant image: `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=60`.

tara: taking over monitoring at 02:13. jamie — ping here when you step out or if you need me to page SRE lead.

marcos: thanks everyone — filing this as a decision log: swap-surge escalation windows shortened for tonight. I'll draft a quick postmortem skeleton if the issue reappears.

sre-bot: [NOTE] Please remember to add incident tags: #swap-surge, #midnight-window. Use `incident-cli add-tag inc-20260304-81 swap-surge`.

marcos: done.

jamie: leaving handoff note at 02:18: p95 stabilized ~3.2s, errors ~0.6%, scaled replicas 10, route fallback active, watching for OOM. handing to tara.

tara: acked and taking over. decided to keep the fallback route for an additional 15m while we watch error trends. will escalate per the swap-surge window if no improvement. :eyes:

marcos: last: if anyone notices pager bindings not firing correctly for scheduled swaps, file a runbook issue. we should automate the swap-surge pager overrides in the roster system to avoid manual confusion.

-- End of thread --
